brief:
FICTIONAL TEST: Maple Street Barbers, a neighbourhood barber shop. Audience: regular customers who book online.
Problem: some booked customers don't turn up, so a barber's chair sits empty at a busy time.
Cause: the only confirmation is an email sent at booking, often days earlier, and it gets buried under other notifications.
Solution: a text the day before that the customer can reply to if they can't make it.
Outcome: when someone replies, the shop can offer that chair time to someone on the walk-in list.
End on a checklist card that says: Reply if you can't make it.
About 15 seconds.

checks: Revision applied: the brief now ends on a checklist card reading 'Reply if you can't make it'. Story, style, cast and layout are unchanged.
Facts come only from the brief. There are no digits, prices, times of day, stats or customer quotes, and none of the forbidden words.
All six essential facts are present, so there are no questions.
The narration is drafted at 34 words in total (9 + 6 + 19), which fits about 15 seconds. It is in the owner's voice and keeps 'can' for the outcome.
Timing: the checklist is the only event on the final word 'walk-in', so the video ends on the card. The dashed connection moves forward to 'chair', after the walk-in person is drawn on 'offer'.
Show, don't label: a real chair, phone, calendar and person. No steps diagram is used.
Each thing is drawn once. The email, text and reply are all messages on the one phone.
The outcome is shown only as possible: the calendar goes to 'available' (not rebooked), the chair stays 'empty', and the walk-in has a dashed link only.
Four objects. The 2x1 chair and the 1x2 phone carry the story; the person and calendar are 1x1. The checklist card sits below the grid automatically.
No overlaps: chair r1c1-r1c2, phone r1c3-r2c3, person r3c1, calendar r3c3. r2c1 is free between the chair and the person for the 'Walk-in list' label.
The callout is on the chair, which sits in row 1.
Every 'on' word is copied from its own chapter's narration: chair, empty, busy, email, buried, text, before, Reply, can, offer, chair, walk-in.
Each object is drawn before it is changed or connected.
Text limits: kickers up to 20, headline lines up to 20, callout 22, messages up to 32, connection label 12, checklist 26.
No em or en dashes are used.
